source.note: The source is this repository's own Python implementation, not a second checkout. Cadenza is being rewritten in place (cadenza#8): `src/cadenza/` and `tests/` are the specification until a later PR retires them, so every inventory here is collected from the working tree at the recorded revision.

file.note: 13 test functions, 14 collected node ids: `test_a_syntax_error_surfaces_as_a_catalog_error_naming_the_file` is parametrized over the two filenames.

systematic_mappings.why: Node ships no TOML parser. Writing one was rejected: none of these 14 cases would notice a hand-rolled parser disagreeing with `tomllib` about escapes, integers or dotted keys, so the ledger would stay green over a parser that read catalogs differently from the specification's. `smol-toml` is TOML 1.0.0 conformant and has no dependencies of its own. The known disagreements are listed under `inherited_limitations`; the choice is recorded in DECISIONS.md and the version is pinned in `package-lock.json` (D-0004).

The nearest equivalent, with one addition the source does not need: the created path is lexically normalised with the port's own `normpath`, because `mkdtempSync` can return a path through a symlink (`/var` -> `/private/var` on macOS) while the adapter reports the string it was given. Resolving it instead would have been the wrong repair -- the adapter deliberately never resolves.
systematic_mappings.affects: the ten cases that touch a filesystem

systematic_mappings.from: `pathlib.Path` as the type of a directory, an origin and a base_dir
systematic_mappings.why: `Path` carries flavour-specific behaviour that `node:path` does not reproduce, and the values here end up inside `LayerDocument.baseDir`, which anchors a `local_path` that reaches a persisted digest. Porting the operations was the alternative to porting the class, and it is the smaller surface.

ids: test/adapters/toml-loader.test.ts::TomlCatalogSource > a byte-order mark is not swallowed
target_only_tests.why: One test, raised by Codex review. `tomllib` sees the U+FEFF that `bytes.decode("utf-8")` leaves in place and refuses a BOM-prefixed catalog at line 1; `TextDecoder` strips a leading BOM unless `ignoreBOM: true` says otherwise, so the port accepted a file the reference implementation rejects. No source case covers it because in Python there is nothing to cover -- the standard library simply does not strip it. Declared here rather than mapped, because it translates no source case. The port's `os.path`/`pathlib` reimplementation is likewise asserted in `test/domain/python-path.test.ts`, which is declared target-only in `parity/target-only.json`: those are claims about the standard library the port had to rebuild, not about `tests/test_toml_loader.py`.

inherited_limitations.behaviour: `smol-toml` and `tomllib` are known to disagree twice, and neither disagreement is reachable by any case in this file. (1) An integer outside JavaScript's safe range is a parse ERROR for `smol-toml` and an ordinary arbitrary-precision `int` for `tomllib`, so such a file becomes `invalid TOML` here and composes there. (2) A float and an integer of the same value are one number in JavaScript, so `schema_version = 1.0` parses to `1` and is ACCEPTED here, where `tomllib` yields a float that section 5.2 refuses.
inherited_limitations.why: The second is a defect in the port under D-0001's oracle order -- design doc section 5.2 says a non-integer is refused -- and it is not closable at this layer: the distinction is destroyed by the parser before the composer sees the value, and recovering it would mean re-lexing the TOML. It is raised for a decision rather than transcribed silently, and `parity/compose.ledger.json` carries the full finding on the source case that exposed it. The first is a divergence in the refusing direction on a value no catalog has a use for, and is recorded so that the belt that meets it does not have to rediscover it.

inherited_limitations.behaviour: Invalid UTF-8 in a layer file raises a decoding failure that is NOT a `CatalogError`, so it escapes this adapter untyped.
inherited_limitations.why: Faithful to the source, which has the same hole: `tomllib.load` decodes the bytes itself, and a `UnicodeDecodeError` is neither a `TOMLDecodeError` nor an `OSError`, so `_read`'s two `except` clauses both miss it. The port uses a fatal `TextDecoder` to keep the behaviour rather than quietly substituting U+FFFD, which would have handed a corrupted catalog to the composer -- a worse failure than the untyped one, and a silent one.

inherited_limitations.behaviour: `os.path.abspath` on Windows calls `_getfullpathname`, which consults a per-drive current directory, so `C:relative` resolves against the CWD of drive C rather than the process CWD.
inherited_limitations.why: Node exposes no per-drive CWD. The one part of `_getfullpathname` that a catalog can plausibly reach -- a drive-less rooted path such as `\srv` picking up the current drive -- IS reproduced; the per-drive case is not, and no case in this file uses one.

inherited_limitations.behaviour: FINDING, raised rather than fixed. On Windows a `local_path` of `/srv/repo` -- rooted but drive-less -- passes `os.path.isabs`, so it is NOT anchored to the layer file's directory, and `os.path.normpath` yields the drive-RELATIVE `\srv\repo`. If the layer's `allowed_local_roots` are drive-less in the same way, containment succeeds and `LocalPathSource.path` is stored drive-relative -- which its own docstring calls "the lexically normalised absolute path", and which a later process on another drive would resolve somewhere else.
inherited_limitations.why: It is NOT a defect in the port: `src/cadenza/domain/clone_source.py` does exactly the same thing, verified by driving `parse_clone_source` with the `ntpath`/`PureWindowsPath` flavours -- it accepts the same input and stores the same `\srv\repo`. Under D-0001 the port agrees with the second and third authorities, and what it disagrees with is the docstring's word "absolute" and the intent of design doc section 3.1. docs/porting.md section 2 says a finding is recorded and raised, NOT transcribed and NOT silently repaired: repairing it here would make the port refuse a catalog the specification accepts, on the Windows cell only, with no ported case and no oracle face covering the change. Recorded for the belt that ports `tests/test_clone_source.py` (57 cases, which own `parse_clone_source`) and raised to the 窓口 for a decision on the Python side.

entries.reason: Same assertion: order is the whole contract between this adapter and the composer.

entries.target_id: test/adapters/toml-loader.test.ts::TomlCatalogSource > each document carries its origin and base dir
entries.reason: Same assertion on all four values. Adapted because `Path` becomes a string: `document.base_dir == tmp_path` compares two `Path` objects and `toBe` compares two strings, so the fixture path is lexically normalised once when it is created -- with the same `normpath` the adapter uses, never with a call that resolves symlinks. Without that, `mkdtempSync` on macOS returns a path through `/var` while the adapter reports the same string it was given, and the case would fail for a reason that has nothing to do with the adapter.

entries.target_id: test/adapters/toml-loader.test.ts::TomlCatalogSource > a directory where the tracked file should be is not mistaken for one
entries.reason: Same assertion: `Path.is_file()` is false for a directory, and `statSync(...).isFile()` is the same question. The port also reproduces pathlib's swallowing of every `OSError`, which `statSync` does not do by itself.

entries.target_id: test/adapters/toml-loader.test.ts::TomlCatalogSource > the repository catalog loads and composes
entries.reason: Same assertion: the file shipped in `config/` is valid input. The one end-to-end case, and the one place a TOML parser disagreeing with `tomllib` about a real catalog would show.

entries.target_id: test/adapters/toml-loader.test.ts::TomlCatalogSource > a relative directory still yields an absolute anchor
entries.reason: Same assertion: the adapter is the one component allowed to consult the CWD, and only to find the files. Adapted because `monkeypatch.chdir` has no counterpart -- `process.chdir` is restored in a `finally` instead, which is safe here because vitest gives each file its own worker and does not run cases within a file concurrently. `Path(...).is_absolute()` becomes `isPathlibAbsolute`, which is the pathlib question and not the `os.path` one; on Windows they differ and this case wants the stricter.

entries.target_id: test/adapters/toml-loader.test.ts::TomlCatalogSource > a layer document refuses a relative base dir
entries.reason: Same assertion. Adapted in the exception type: the source raises a bare `ValueError` from `__post_init__` and the port raises `RangeError`, JavaScript's nearest equivalent -- the type is right and the value is not. Deliberately NOT a `CadenzaError`, which matches the source: design doc section 7 governs catalog refusals that name a file an operator can edit, and this is a class invariant broken by a caller inside cadenza.

Same assertions, per project: a non-empty base branch, and no project listing its own id as an alias. Adapted in the guard: the source writes `assert catalog.projects` before the loop, and the port asserts a count greater than zero, because a loop over an empty collection passes while proving nothing and a truthiness check on an object is always true in JavaScript. Probed by emptying the collection, which turns the case red as it should.

entries.target_id: test/adapters/toml-loader.test.ts::TomlCatalogSource > a drive-less path is not absolute on windows
entries.reason: Same assertion, and the same reason for existing: it explains why `test/support.ts` builds absolute paths from a platform anchor instead of writing `/srv/...`. Adapted because `PureWindowsPath` and `PurePosixPath` become the two flavour objects of `src/domain/python-path.ts`, which is the port's way of holding both answers at once -- the same thing pathlib's flavours are.
